task: Repair the existing Plan Before Code gate so a critical proof-only transaction whose projected files are exclusively neutral/test or knowledge-infrastructure paths may truthfully declare an empty domain/authority projection, while preserving exact scope drift detection whenever any architecture-bearing projected file exists.

operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: The final Brabus rehearsal proved a contradiction in the existing Plan Before Code gate. A critical proof-only plan can legitimately project only neutral test files, yielding projectedDomains=[] and projectedAuthorities=[], yet the gate unconditionally requires both declared arrays to be non-empty while also requiring exact equality with the empty projection. Such a transaction therefore cannot pass without falsely claiming an unrelated architecture domain. The repair must preserve the existing gate and exact drift checks, but make non-empty declaration mandatory only when the projection actually contains an architecture-bearing non-neutral file.
observableOutcomes: A critical plan with only neutral/test projected files may declare expectedDomains=[] and expectedAuthorities=[] without DEV_PLAN_EXPECTED_*_REQUIRED.
Exact projected-vs-declared domain and authority equality remains enforced.
A critical plan that projects any architecture-bearing non-neutral file still requires non-empty expectedDomains and expectedAuthorities.
Knowledge-infrastructure or neutral-only proof transactions are not forced to fabricate Builder, Storefront or other product authority ownership.
No Release Risk, Completion Truth, Atlas architecture resolution or external proof rule is weakened.
The final Brabus rehearsal can remain a proof-only transaction rather than adding fake product code solely to satisfy the planner.
unresolvedRisks: The relaxation could accidentally allow a real product-code plan to omit domain/authority declarations.
Knowledge infrastructure could be misclassified as neutral even when a canonical domain is projected.
The change could weaken exact scope drift checks instead of only changing the non-empty prerequisite.
A test-only plan could hide an unresolved architecture-bearing file through broad globbing.

in: Conditional non-empty expectedDomains/expectedAuthorities validation in the existing Plan Before Code gate.
Use the gate's existing isNeutralFile and knowledgeInfrastructurePrefixes semantics to distinguish proof-only from architecture-bearing projections.
Regression tests for neutral/test-only critical plans and architecture-bearing critical plans.
out: Changes to Release Risk Budget thresholds or subsystem policy.
Changes to Completion Truth or Template Factory evidence requirements.
Any Template #3 or rehearsal product implementation.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: This change affects the planner that authorizes critical development transactions. The highest practical assurance is a minimal conditional around the existing requirement, exact drift checks left unchanged, explicit adversarial tests proving neutral-only allowance and product-code fail-closed behavior, and full existing quality/type/build verification.

acceptanceCriteria: The gate computes whether projectedFiles contain at least one architecture-bearing file using existing neutral/knowledge-infrastructure semantics.
DEV_PLAN_EXPECTED_DOMAINS_REQUIRED is emitted only when an architecture-bearing projected file exists and expectedDomains is empty.
DEV_PLAN_EXPECTED_AUTHORITIES_REQUIRED is emitted only when an architecture-bearing projected file exists and expectedAuthorities is empty.
DEV_PLAN_DOMAIN_SCOPE_DRIFT and DEV_PLAN_AUTHORITY_SCOPE_DRIFT remain unconditional exact-equality checks.
A synthetic critical neutral/test-only projection with empty expected arrays passes the non-empty prerequisite.
A synthetic critical product-code projection with empty expected arrays remains blocked.
The fix does not alter subsystem, Known Failure, Negative Knowledge, PO instruction, Release Risk or Completion Truth logic.
invariants: No fabricated architecture ownership is required for neutral-only proof transactions.
Architecture-bearing transactions still declare explicit domain and authority ownership.

failureModes: A neutral-only critical plan remains impossible because the unconditional non-empty checks survive.
A real source file is treated as neutral and bypasses required ownership declaration.
The fix skips exact equality and allows declared scope to diverge from Atlas projection.
The regression test only checks source strings and never exercises the decision predicate.
edgeCases: Projected files contain only knowledge-infrastructure scripts.
Projected files mix a neutral test with a Builder source file.
Projected files are neutral while actual diff currently contains only active-plan metadata.
Expected arrays are empty and projected domains are empty.
Expected arrays are empty while projected domains are non-empty.

alternatives.summary: Require non-empty domain/authority declarations only when architecture-bearing projected files exist.
alternatives.reason: Preserves exact ownership enforcement while allowing truthful proof-only critical transactions.

alternatives.summary: Declare DOMAIN-BUILDER/builder-template-system for a test-only rehearsal.
alternatives.reason: Would deliberately make plan metadata false and undermine the authority graph.

alternatives.summary: Add or touch Builder code solely to create a non-empty projection.
alternatives.reason: Would pollute release scope and create meaningless implementation change.

specialistReviews.finding: Critical plans normally must declare authority ownership; allowing empty arrays must not become a general bypass.
specialistReviews.resolution: Condition the prerequisite on architecture-bearing projected files and retain unconditional exact drift comparison.

specialistReviews.finding: The observed contradiction is deterministic: empty Atlas projection plus unconditional non-empty declaration cannot both be satisfied truthfully.
specialistReviews.resolution: Use the same neutral/knowledge-infrastructure classification already trusted by unresolved-scope logic.

specialistReviews.finding: The fix should not touch storefront or template runtime behavior.
specialistReviews.resolution: Restrict implementation to the existing planner and its regression test.

specialistReviews.finding: The prerequisite must remain separate from #795 so rehearsal scope is not mixed with Control Plane infrastructure.
specialistReviews.resolution: Use a dedicated stacked prerequisite branch and retarget/rebase the rehearsal only after lifecycle closure.

challenge.scenario: Critical plan projects only tests and expected domain/authority arrays are empty.
challenge.finding: Current gate emits REQUIRED despite zero projected architecture ownership.
challenge.resolution: After fix, non-empty prerequisite is skipped but exact empty==empty drift checks still run.

challenge.scenario: Critical plan projects src/lib/builder/storefront-runtime.ts with empty declarations.
challenge.finding: This must never gain the neutral-only exception.
challenge.resolution: Architecture-bearing predicate is true and both REQUIRED findings remain.

challenge.scenario: Critical plan mixes one test and one Builder source file.
challenge.finding: Presence of any architecture-bearing file must preserve strict declaration.
challenge.resolution: Predicate is true for the mixed projection; empty declarations block.

challenge.scenario: Expected domain is fabricated while projection is empty.
challenge.finding: Skipping the REQUIRED check alone must not allow false metadata.

challenge.scenario: Only a knowledge-infrastructure script is planned.
challenge.finding: It may be architecturally classified but also belongs to the planner's special infrastructure set.
challenge.resolution: The non-empty prerequisite uses existing special classification while exact projected ownership equality remains authoritative.

challenge.scenario: Broad test glob accidentally captures a non-neutral source path.
challenge.finding: A bypass based on glob text rather than resolved projected files would be unsafe.
challenge.resolution: Evaluate the actual projectedFiles list item-by-item using canonical predicates.

challenge.scenario: The fix changes release risk or truth behavior indirectly.
challenge.finding: A planner repair must not weaken downstream assurance.
challenge.resolution: No downstream gate file or policy is modified; full quality/build proof remains required.

challenge.scenario: Final Brabus rehearsal retries after prerequisite closure.
challenge.finding: It must pass Plan only because its projection is honestly neutral, not because Builder ownership was fabricated.
challenge.resolution: Retarget rehearsal to the closed prerequisite and declare empty domain/authority projection with measured subsystems.

proofPlan: Plan Before Code on this prerequisite validates its own Quality-domain scope before code change.
Regression test asserts the planner contains an explicit architecture-bearing projection predicate rather than removing REQUIRED findings.
Adversarial regression proves neutral-only empty ownership is allowed while mixed/product-code empty ownership remains blocked.
Source scan proves exact DOMAIN_SCOPE_DRIFT and AUTHORITY_SCOPE_DRIFT comparisons remain unconditional.
Incremental replay, Release Risk, full Quality tests, TypeScript, Production Build and Completion Truth run normally.
After lifecycle closure, #795 is rebased/retargeted onto this prerequisite and reruns its original Plan gates.

requirements.requirement: Critical proof-only plans with exclusively neutral or knowledge-infrastructure projections can truthfully use empty domain/authority declarations without bypassing exact scope drift checks.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Architecture-bearing critical plans cannot pass with empty expectedDomains/expectedAuthorities.
